long_biography.plain_text:
Historic rehabilitation became a defining part of David Corsetti's work after he bought Providence's Henry A. Kirby House in the late 1990s. The young developer underestimated the restoration's capital and labour demands, but completed the four-year project and earned a local preservation award in 2002.

That experience informed Corsetti's work on larger industrial buildings through Premier Land Development. The seven-year redevelopment of Wanskuck Mill returned a neglected Providence landmark to use as housing and commercial space, earning a Rhody Award. He argues that existing mill structures can shorten approvals and reduce some construction costs, while state and federal historic tax credits help close financing gaps. The Ann and Hope Mill project converts another historic industrial complex into housing in Cumberland.
